subject: Hosted API pricing — traffic & budget follow-up
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@lynxai.com>, Procurement <procurement@lynxai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: hosted API pricing — traffic & budget clarifications

Alex / Procurement team — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few specific asks so we can finalize a pricing proposal and an ops runbook for the POC.

Highlights from our discovery:
- Primary use case: document summarization + chat layer tied to product support flows.
- Target go-live: production in Jan 2027, POC in Oct 2026.
- Integration: standard Redwood REST SDK, streaming not required for first phase.

Open items we need from you (short answers are OK):
1) Expected monthly token volume (range is fine): low / expected / high (e.g., 5M / 25M / 50M).
2) Target unit economics: ideal $/1M tokens you are budgeting for (or range).
3) Peak TPS profile: baseline TPS vs burst TPS (duration of bursts).
4) Request token sizes: average tokens in / out or % short vs % long.
5) Procurement timeline and whether you prefer committed monthly minimums (term discounts) or a pure consumption model.

We attached our current pricing bands (redwood_pricing_bands_v2.pdf) so you have a point of reference; happy to adjust to match your volume profile. If you can send the spreadsheet with your traffic estimate, Ben and I will return a concrete price/term proposal within 24 hours.

Next steps proposed:
- Alex: send the volume spreadsheet and any procurement constraints (by end of day Friday).
- We’ll come back with two options: (A) consumption-based estimate, (B) committed 12mo term with discount and burst capacity.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
irene@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: redwood_pricing_bands_v2.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Alex Moreno <alex@lynxai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@lynxai.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: hosted API pricing — traffic & budget clarifications

Thanks, Irene — quick answers below and I attached our internal estimate workbook. Happy to hop on a short follow-up if anything needs clarifying.

1) Monthly tokens (Q4 forecast -> first-year production):
- Low: 25,000,000 tokens/month
- Expected: 32,000,000 tokens/month
- High: 40,000,000 tokens/month

2) Target unit economics: we’re budgeting roughly $700–900 per 1M tokens, our procurement target is ~$800/1M tokens for the initial contract.

3) Peak TPS: baseline around 40 TPS. Predictable daily peaks to ~120 TPS. We anticipate occasional traffic spikes up to ~220 TPS for ~3–7 minutes during product launches.

4) Token sizes / distribution: average tokens per full request (input+output) ~450 tokens. Breakdown: ~60% short interactions (<256 tokens), ~40% longer (512–1500 tokens) for summarization jobs.

5) Procurement: leaning toward a committed discount structure if the price aligns with our budget. Procurement timeline: intent to sign term sheet by mid-Nov (internal procurement review in Oct).

Attached: lynx_volume_estimate_q3.xlsx (Excel, 48KB) — contains per-endpoint traffic slices and peak-minute estimates.

Let me know if you want the raw sample prompts we used for tokenization — can share a sanitized version.

—Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Platform Engineering | LynxAI
alex@lynxai.com | +1 (646) 555-1992
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@lynxai.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: hosted API pricing — traffic & budget clarifications

Alex — really helpful, thanks for the numbers and the workbook. Drafting two concrete options (short summary below) and I’ll attach a draft term sheet for internal review.

Option A — Consumption (no long-term commit):
- List price band we’d apply: $1,000 / 1M tokens (standard hosted API)
- Autoscaling & prefix caching included; support package: Standard (email + access to runbooks)
- Good if Lynx wants maximum flexibility; cost likely above your target without commit.

Option B — Committed 12-month term (example):
- Commit: 30M tokens / month (12 months)
- Effective unit price: $750 / 1M tokens for committed usage
- Overage: $850 / 1M tokens for usage above commit in each month
- Included: 99.9% uptime SLA, priority support, reserved baseline capacity to meet 120 TPS, burst headroom up to 220 TPS subject to capacity scheduling

Quick notes on economics: with your expected 32M/month profile, the committed option lands ~ $24k/month vs consumption ~$32k/month at list — aligns with your ~$800/1M target if we structure a 12mo term and a 30M commit. We can also model a 6mo variant if that helps procurement.

Next asks from our side:
- Confirm whether Lynx can commit to a 30M minimum (or propose a different number).
- If you have sample prompts or a small prompt set (sanitized), our ops team will run a tokenization pass to verify the average token estimates.

Attaching: draft_term_sheet.pdf for review (internal/external redlines welcome). I’ll also create a HubSpot deal and link it to the DocuSign envelope once we agree on commit.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
ben@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0188

Attachment: draft_term_sheet.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: ops checklist before term proposal

Internal note (do not forward externally) — a few ops/engineering items we should validate before finalizing the term:

1) Tokenization audit: we need the sanitized sample prompts Alex mentioned so we can confirm the 450 token average. Small differences can swing monthly spend materially.
2) Traffic shaping: confirm whether the 220 TPS spikes coincide with other customers’ launches in the same region; if so we may recommend a scheduled burst reservation.
3) P95 latency target: clarify whether Lynx expects <300ms p95 for short interactions — we should get this on record for SLA sizing.
4) Logging/audit: procurement asked about retention; they need 6 months of request logs for compliance — confirm if that’s acceptable or if they need a longer retention package.

I attached an ops runbook template to capture RBAC, incident contacts, and escalation for the POC. Ben/Irene — once Alex shares prompts and confirms commit cadence (monthly true-up vs front-loaded), I’ll complete the SLO page and ops attachments for the term sheet.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: ops_runbook_template.md (text/markdown)
